title: Event 1
content:
Summary Report: “AWS Cloud and AI Day Hanoi 2026” Event Information Event name: AWS Cloud and AI Day Hanoi 2026 Date & time: Tuesday, 29/09/2026, 07:30 – 17:00 (UTC+7) Main venue: JW Marriott Hotel Hanoi Where I attended: HCMC Watch Party – AWS Vietnam office, Ho Chi Minh City (live stream of the keynote and selected sessions) Role: Attendee Event page: https://aws.amazon.com/vi/events/cloud-day-hanoi/ Event Objectives Show how AWS helps builders turn ideas into real products with cloud and AI Introduce agentic AI (AI agents that can plan and carry out tasks) for developers, workload modernization and security Share real customer stories from Vietnamese companies Connect developers, IT leaders and the AWS community in Vietnam Keynote Speakers H.E. Jennifer Wicks – U.S. Ambassador to Vietnam Dr. Werner Vogels – CTO, Amazon.com Eric Yeo – Country General Manager Malaysia, Vietnam, Indochina, AWS Mai Le – Director of Product Management, Katalon Dr. Jens Lottner – Chief Executive Officer, Techcombank Sessions I Attended Time Session Level 09:00 Keynote – What does it take to solve problems everyone says are impossible? (KEY001) 200 11:00 Building software like never before with agentic AI (DVT205 – HCMC Watch Party) 300 11:00 (Hanoi) Build an AI-ready data foundation (ANT202) / Migration at Scale with Agentic AI: AWS Transform and Beyond (AIM302) 200 / 300 Key Highlights Keynote: making “impossible” ideas possible AWS presented how its tools and resources help builders go beyond their limits, with experiences from customers such as Techcombank and Katalon. A big theme was agentic systems: AI agents that support developers, help modernize workloads and help keep organizations secure. Agentic AI for software development AI is moving from “suggesting code” to agents that can take a task, plan the steps and carry them out (write code, write tests, fix errors). The developer’s role shifts toward describing the problem clearly, reviewing the agent’s output and making the final decisions. AI-ready data foundation An AI application is only as good as its data: data needs to be collected, cleaned, organized and governed before it can be used by AI. The cloud provides managed services for storing and analyzing data so teams can focus on using it instead of maintaining infrastructure. Migration at scale with AWS Transform AWS Transform uses agentic AI to speed up migrating and modernizing large, old systems, a job that normally takes a lot of manual work. Key Takeaways AI is now a practical tool in real Vietnamese businesses, not just a research topic. Good AI starts with good data and a solid cloud foundation (security, cost control, monitoring). As an AI student, I need to learn both AI and cloud: models are only useful when they are deployed, monitored and secured in a real system. Applying to My Work Use the idea of an AI-ready data flow (upload → process → store → use) when designing our team’s capstone workshop. Prefer managed / serverless AWS services so the team can focus on the AI features instead of managing servers. Try AI coding assistants carefully: use them to speed up work, but always read and understand the generated code. Event Experience This was my first large AWS event. Watching the keynote and sessions together with other FCAJ interns at the HCMC Watch Party helped me see how cloud and AI are used by real companies in Vietnam. Many terms were new to me (agentic AI, data foundation, AWS Transform), so I noted them down to study further during the internship.

title: Proposal
content:
SmartDoc – AI-Powered Invoice Processing on AWS Serverless Status: Proposal v1.0 (28/10/2026). The official architecture diagram will be drawn by the team in draw.io using the AWS Architecture Icons and added to Section 4.
1. Overview SmartDoc is a serverless web application that helps small businesses, shops, student groups and individuals digitize paper invoices and receipts from a single photo. A user signs in and uploads a photo of an invoice. The system then uses the multimodal AI model Amazon Nova Lite on Amazon Bedrock to read the content, extract key fields (vendor, date, total, tax, line items), classify the expense (food, transport, office supplies, …) and write a short summary. Results are stored in Amazon DynamoDB and shown back in the web UI within seconds.
The whole system follows an event-driven, serverless architecture: there are no servers to manage, and the team pays only for actual usage.
2. Problem Statement Small businesses and individuals still receive many paper invoices and receipts (restaurants, supermarkets, taxis, office supplies). Typing each one into Excel by hand is slow and error-prone, and paper receipts are easily lost. Traditional OCR tools return only raw text, so users still have to find the total and the date and categorize each expense themselves. Invoices in Vietnam are mostly in Vietnamese with diacritics and come in many layouts, so a fixed template does not work well. Solution: use a multimodal AI model that reads and understands an invoice in one step and returns structured data (JSON) for storage, search and reporting.
3. Objectives & Scope 3.1. Objectives Build an automated pipeline, Upload → AI extraction → Storage → Display, that runs entirely on AWS. Apply the AWS Well-Architected Framework, especially the Security pillar (IAM least privilege, no public resources, no hard-coded credentials). Provide full observability with Amazon CloudWatch (Logs, Metrics, Alarms) and email alerts through Amazon SNS. Keep operating cost below USD 2/month under a realistic workload (Section 6). Write a bilingual step-by-step guide that lets others reproduce the deployment. 3.2. Success Criteria Criterion Target End-to-end processing time per invoice (upload → result) ≤ 15 seconds Extraction accuracy for total and date on a 30-invoice test set ≥ 85% API calls without signing in Rejected (HTTP 401) User A reading User B’s data Not possible Processing errors (corrupt image, malformed AI output) Logged, marked FAILED, email alert sent Direct Internet access to S3 buckets Blocked (Block Public Access) 3.3. Scope In scope Out of scope Single-page invoice/receipt images (JPG/PNG, ≤ 5 MB) Multi-page PDFs Key-field extraction, classification, summary Integration with accounting software or e-invoices (XML) Sign-up/sign-in with Amazon Cognito Multiple roles (admin, accountant, …) List and detail views of the user’s own invoices Advanced reporting, Excel export Single Region: us-east-1 Multi-Region, disaster recovery 4. Solution Architecture 4.1. AWS Services and Rationale Service Role in the system Why it was chosen Amazon S3 (1) Stores invoice images (private bucket); (2) hosts the static website 99.999999999% durability, low cost, emits S3 Events to trigger processing Amazon CloudFront Serves the static site over HTTPS and reads S3 through Origin Access Control (OAC) The website bucket stays private; free HTTPS; covered by the Always Free tier (1 TB/month) Amazon Cognito (User Pool) Sign-up, sign-in, issues JWT tokens Managed identity, free up to 10,000 MAU, the app never stores passwords Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API) REST endpoints for the web app, protected by a Cognito JWT authorizer Cheaper than REST APIs (~USD 1 per million requests), native Cognito integration AWS Lambda (Python 3.12) Three functions: presign-upload, process-document, get-documents Serverless, pay per invocation, scales automatically Amazon Bedrock – Amazon Nova Lite Reads the invoice image, extracts JSON, classifies, summarizes Multimodal (accepts images), very low price (USD 0.06 per 1M input tokens), available in-Region in us-east-1 Amazon DynamoDB (On-demand) Stores extraction results per user Serverless NoSQL, pay per request, low latency, 25 GB free Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) for failed processing events No data loss on failure; events can be reprocessed Amazon CloudWatch Logs, metrics (built-in + custom), alarms, dashboard Centralized monitoring, required by the workshop Amazon SNS Sends email when an alarm fires Simple; 1,000 emails/month free AWS IAM One dedicated least-privilege IAM role per Lambda function Security foundation of the whole system Why not Amazon Textract? The team first planned to use Textract for OCR, but research showed that (1) on a new AWS account on the Free plan, Textract is only available after upgrading to the Paid plan, and (2) Textract does not support Vietnamese, while most invoices in Vietnam are in Vietnamese. The multimodal Nova Lite model handles both reading and understanding, so the architecture is simpler and cheaper.
4.2. Data Flow The user opens the website through CloudFront, signs in with Cognito and receives a JWT token. The web app calls POST /upload-url on API Gateway with the token. API Gateway validates the token with the JWT authorizer and invokes the presign-upload Lambda. presign-upload creates a PENDING record in DynamoDB and returns a presigned URL (a temporary upload link that expires after 5 minutes) for the key uploads/{userId}/{documentId}.jpg. The browser uploads the image directly to S3 with the presigned URL, so the image never passes through Lambda or API Gateway. S3 emits an ObjectCreated event (only for the uploads/ prefix), which asynchronously invokes the process-document Lambda. process-document reads the image from S3, calls the Bedrock Converse API with Nova Lite and a prompt that asks for JSON output, validates the JSON, and updates DynamoDB to DONE (or FAILED on error). If the Lambda still fails after 2 retries, the event is sent to the SQS DLQ. The web app calls GET /documents. The get-documents Lambda queries DynamoDB only by the userId taken from the token and returns the results. Every Lambda writes logs and metrics to CloudWatch; alarms send emails through SNS when errors occur. 4.3. Security Design (Security Pillar) Principle How SmartDoc applies it Least privilege Each Lambda has its own role. For example, process-document may only call s3:GetObject on uploads/*, bedrock:InvokeModel on exactly one Nova Lite model and dynamodb:UpdateItem on exactly one table. presign-upload may only call s3:PutObject on uploads/*. No * in actions or resources No public resources Both buckets have Block Public Access enabled. The website bucket is readable only by CloudFront via OAC. The image bucket accepts uploads only through short-lived presigned URLs Authentication & data isolation Every API requires a Cognito JWT. userId always comes from the token’s sub claim, never from client input, so users cannot read each other’s data No hard-coded credentials Lambdas use IAM roles (temporary credentials issued by AWS). Bucket, table and model names are passed as environment variables. The GitHub repository contains no access keys and has a .gitignore Encryption S3 and DynamoDB encrypt data at rest by default; all traffic uses HTTPS/TLS Input protection Presigned URLs restrict the image Content-Type; the Lambda rejects files > 5 MB; AI output is validated before it is stored AI data privacy According to AWS documentation, Bedrock does not use customer prompts or outputs to train models Why are the Lambdas not placed in a VPC/private subnet? The system has no database or server that needs a private network. The Lambdas reach S3, DynamoDB and Bedrock over HTTPS, authenticated by IAM. Putting them in a VPC would add NAT Gateway or interface VPC endpoint charges (tens of USD per month) without a meaningful security gain for this architecture. The team lists it as a future extension if compliance requires it.
4.4. Mapping to the AWS Well-Architected Framework Pillar Application Operational Excellence CloudWatch Logs (14-day retention), dashboard, alarms; a reproducible deployment guide Security See Section 4.3 Reliability Event-driven design; Lambda retries twice automatically; the DLQ keeps failed events; clear PENDING/DONE/FAILED states Performance Efficiency Direct-to-S3 uploads with presigned URLs; a small, fast model (Nova Lite); key-based DynamoDB queries Cost Optimization 100% serverless, pay per use; S3 Lifecycle deletes images after 30 days; 14-day log retention; AWS Budgets alerts Sustainability No idle resources; compute is used only when an invoice needs processing 5. Plan & Timeline Internship period: 14/09/2026 – 04/12/2026. Planned workshop submission deadline: 19/11/2026 (15 days before the internship certificate is needed).
5.1. Roles Member Main responsibility Member A Team lead, integration, IAM & security Member B process-document Lambda, Bedrock prompt, accuracy evaluation Member C Cognito, API Gateway, presign-upload and get-documents Lambdas Member D Static web UI, S3 + CloudFront (OAC) Member E CloudWatch, SNS, DLQ, cost estimation, clean-up guide Every member must understand the whole architecture and be able to explain all of it, not only their own part.
5.2. Weekly Timeline Internship week Dates Tasks Output Week 7 28/10 – 01/11 Finalize topic and write the proposal; test Nova Lite in the Bedrock playground with 10 sample invoices; collect 30 test invoices; sketch the architecture diagram Proposal, prompt v1, test dataset Week 8 02/11 – 08/11 Create S3, DynamoDB and IAM roles; build the process-document Lambda + S3 event; create Cognito, API Gateway and the two API Lambdas Backend pipeline working via CLI/Postman Week 9 09/11 – 15/11 Build the static site + CloudFront; CloudWatch metrics/alarms/dashboard, SNS, DLQ; testing (valid, invalid, error and load cases); AWS Pricing Calculator estimate; record the demo video End-to-end demo, video, cost table Week 10 16/11 – 19/11 Write the bilingual 5-Workshop section (step-by-step, testing, clean-up), take screenshots, finalize the diagram, peer review Submit workshop on 19/11 Week 10–12 20/11 – 04/12 Apply mentor feedback, finish blogs and worklogs, clean up resources Final report 6. Cost Estimation Workload scenario: a small shop processes about 3,000 invoices/month (~100/day), with 1 MB images on average and about 30,000 list/detail views per month. Region us-east-1, on-demand prices, before Free Tier/credits.
Service Assumptions Estimated cost (USD/month) Amazon Bedrock (Nova Lite) 3,000 calls × (~2,000 input + ~500 output tokens) 0.72 AWS Lambda 36,000 invocations, ~16,650 GB-seconds 0.28 (within the 400,000 GB-s free tier) Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API) 33,000 requests 0.03 Amazon DynamoDB (On-demand) 12,000 WRU + 30,000 RRU, < 1 GB 0.01 Amazon S3 3 GB (30-day lifecycle), 3,000 PUT/GET 0.09 Amazon CloudWatch 0.5 GB logs, 3 alarms, 3 custom metrics, 1 dashboard 0.27 (mostly within the free tier) Amazon CloudFront ~2 GB transfer, 40,000 requests 0.00 (Always Free) Amazon Cognito < 10,000 MAU 0.00 Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS A few dozen emails/messages 0.00 Total ≈ USD 1.40/month (≈ USD 17/year) During development and the demo (fewer than 300 invoices expected), Bedrock costs only about USD 0.07, and everything is covered by the USD 200 credit of a new account.
AWS Pricing Calculator link: [to be added after the estimate is created]
Cost Optimization Strategy 100% serverless architecture: no EC2, NAT Gateway or always-on resources. Use Nova Lite instead of a larger model; cap output maxTokens; resize images before upload (max ~1,400 px) to reduce tokens. S3 Lifecycle policy deletes original images after 30 days (extracted data stays in DynamoDB). 14-day CloudWatch Logs retention instead of the default “Never expire”. HTTP API instead of REST API (about 70% cheaper). AWS Budgets alert at USD 5; run the clean-up right after grading. 7. Risks & Mitigation Risk Impact Mitigation Nova Lite misreads Vietnamese diacritics or blurry photos Wrong extraction Test 10 images in Week 7; improve the prompt; if still poor, switch to Nova Pro (same API, only the model ID changes) AI returns malformed JSON Lambda failure Validate the JSON and retry once; otherwise mark FAILED and log it Low Bedrock quotas on a new account Throttling during the demo Check Service Quotas early; retry with backoff; demo with moderate load Recursive S3 → Lambda → S3 trigger Runaway cost Trigger only on the uploads/ prefix; the Lambda never writes back to S3 Access keys leaked to GitHub Account compromise Use IAM roles only; .gitignore; review before every commit Unexpected charges Credit loss AWS Budgets + Free plan; clean-up checklist Limited time (~3 weeks) Missing the deadline Build the MVP first, extras later; every week has a clear deliverable Members are still new to AWS Delays; cannot answer the mentor’s questions Learn while building; peer reviews; every member explains the full architecture 8. Expected Outcomes A working web application: sign in → upload an invoice photo → see the extracted fields, category and summary. A monitoring setup with a CloudWatch dashboard, alarms and email alerts. A bilingual workshop guide that can be reproduced from scratch, including testing and clean-up. Hands-on skills for the team: event-driven serverless architecture, IAM least privilege, generative AI on Amazon Bedrock, monitoring and cost optimization on AWS.

title: Week 6 Worklog
content: Week 6 Objectives: Learn Cloud Observability (CloudWatch, CloudTrail, Systems Manager). Learn Serverless Computing with AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Learn Cloud Observability & Monitoring: + Amazon CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms, and Metric Filters + CloudWatch Logs Insights for querying structured logs + AWS CloudTrail for recording and auditing API activity across accounts. 19/10/2026 19/10/2026 https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 3 - Learn Systems Operations with AWS Systems Manager (SSM): + SSM Session Manager (SSH-less secure shell access without opening port 22) + SSM Patch Manager & Run Command for automated fleet maintenance. 20/10/2026 20/10/2026 https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 4 - Learn Serverless Compute with AWS Lambda: + Serverless execution model, triggers, event sources + Lambda execution roles & resource policies + Memory allocation, execution timeouts, and cold start optimizations + Lambda Layers for shared dependency management. 21/10/2026 21/10/2026 https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 5 - Learn Amazon API Gateway: + REST API vs HTTP API architectures + Method Request/Response, Integration Request/Response + Lambda Proxy Integration and CORS configuration + API Gateway Throttling, Usage Plans, and API Keys. 22/10/2026 22/10/2026 https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 6 - Hands-on Lab (planned, not yet practiced): + Build a Serverless CRUD API using API Gateway, AWS Lambda (Python), and Amazon DynamoDB + Implement structured logging to CloudWatch and configure error alerts via SNS. 23/10/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ Week 6 Achievements: Learned the basics of CloudWatch monitoring, CloudTrail logging, and SSM Session Manager. Learned the concept of a Serverless REST API with API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and DynamoDB (hands-on practice pending). Learned how CloudWatch alarms monitor Lambda functions (hands-on practice pending).

title: Week 7 Worklog
content: Week 7 Objectives: Learn Event-Driven Architectures (SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Step Functions). Understand user authentication with Amazon Cognito and publish Technical Blog #2. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Learn Asynchronous Messaging Services: + Amazon SQS: Standard vs FIFO Queues, Visibility Timeout, Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) + Amazon SNS: Pub/Sub Fan-out pattern, Topic Subscriptions (Email, SQS, Lambda). 26/10/2026 26/10/2026 https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 3 - Learn Event-Driven Architecture & Orchestration: + Amazon EventBridge: Event Buses, Event Patterns, Rules, and Partner integrations + AWS Step Functions: State Machines, Task/Choice/Parallel States, Error Handling. 27/10/2026 27/10/2026 https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 4 - Learn Identity & User Management with Amazon Cognito: + Cognito User Pools (User sign-up, sign-in, MFA, Hosted UI) + Cognito Identity Pools (Federated Identities & IAM temporary STS credentials) + JWT Token validation in API Gateway Authorizers. 28/10/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 5 - Practice Hands-on Lab: + Build an Asynchronous Event-Driven Image Processing Pipeline + Architecture: S3 Upload -> EventBridge -> SQS Queue -> Lambda Worker (Thumbnail generation) -> DynamoDB update. 29/10/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 6 - Author & Publish Technical Blog #2: + Topic: ‘Architecting Resilient Event-Driven Systems on AWS using EventBridge, SQS, and Step Functions’ + Share blog post to AWS Study Group community and engage with feedback. 30/10/2026 Ongoing https://workshop-sample.awsfcaj.com/ Week 7 Achievements: Ongoing Ongoing Ongoing

title: Week 8 Worklog
content: Week 8 Objectives: Learn Infrastructure as Code (CloudFormation, CDK, SAM) and CI/CD pipelines. Participate in Community Event #1. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Learn Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with AWS CloudFormation: + Template syntax (JSON/YAML), Parameters, Resources, Outputs, Intrinsic Functions + CloudFormation Stacks, Nested Stacks, and Drift Detection. 02/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 3 - Learn AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK): + CDK Core Concepts: App, Stack, Constructs (L1, L2, L3) + Writing CDK code in TypeScript/Python + CDK CLI commands (cdk init, cdk synth, cdk diff, cdk deploy). 03/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 4 - Learn AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM): + SAM Template specifications (AWS::Serverless::Function, SimpleTable) + SAM CLI local emulation and automated packaging/deployment. 04/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 5 - Learn AWS DevOps CI/CD Services: + AWS CodePipeline for continuous delivery orchestration + AWS CodeBuild for automated unit testing & artifact build (buildspec.yml) + AWS CodeDeploy for automated rolling and blue/green deployments. 05/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 6 - Participate in Community Event #1: + Event: ‘AWS Cloud & DevOps Community Meetup / FCAJ Tech Talk 1’ + Attend technical presentations on modern CI/CD & IaC best practices + Write summary notes and key takeaways for the OJT event report. 06/11/2026 Ongoing https://workshop-sample.awsfcaj.com/ Week 8 Achievements: Ongoing Ongoing Ongoing

title: Week 9 Worklog
content: Week 9 Objectives: Learn Container Services on AWS (Docker, Amazon ECR, Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate). Author and publish Technical Blog #3. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Learn Containerization Fundamentals: + Docker container concepts, images, and container lifecycle + Writing multi-stage, secure Dockerfiles + Building and running containers locally. 09/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 3 - Learn Amazon ECR & Amazon ECS: + Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) for private image storage + Amazon ECS Components: Clusters, Task Definitions, Services + Launch types: EC2 Launch Type vs AWS Fargate (Serverless Containers). 10/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 4 - Learn Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS): + EKS Architecture: Control Plane, Managed Node Groups, Fargate Profiles + kubectl and eksctl management + Pod networking, IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA), and EKS Pod Identity. 11/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 5 - Practice Hands-on Lab: + Containerize a sample web application + Push image to Amazon ECR + Deploy on Amazon ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer with auto-scaling. 12/11/2026 Ongoing https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com/ 6 - Author & Publish Technical Blog #3: + Topic: ‘Deploying Scalable Containerized Microservices with Amazon ECS Fargate and AWS CDK’ + Publish to AWS Study Group and interact with community discussions. 13/11/2026 Ongoing https://workshop-sample.awsfcaj.com/ Week 9 Achievements: Ongoing Ongoing Ongoing
